pred_ddx.label: Granulomatous Lesion of the Urinary Bladder

Urinary Bladder Neoplasm: The patient presents with right flank pain, dysuria, and hematuria, and imaging reveals a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion along the anterosuperior wall of the urinary bladder, consistent with a neoplastic lesion. The presence of a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks and heterogeneous enhancement in the early arterial and venous phases further supports this diagnosis.
Granulomatous Lesion of the Urinary Blad: The patient's symptoms of hematuria and dysuria could be consistent with a granulomatous lesion of the urinary bladder, but the imaging findings are more suggestive of a neoplastic lesion.
